name: Yen & carry trade
summary: Yen near ¥159.0 per dollar on 23 Nov, little changed on the week; no intervention found
state: The dollar was near ¥159.0 early on 23 Nov, down 0.5% on the week and up 1.6% on the month, inside the 3% weekly and 6% monthly Watch lines (Yahoo Finance). The yen is about 3% stronger than its 52-week low. No Japanese currency intervention was found to 23 Nov.
for_you: The yen is weak but moving gradually, with no sign of the sudden unwinding of carry trades that has unsettled markets in the past.
rubric_hit: USD/JPY 1w move 0.53% below the 3% Watch line; USD/JPY 1m move 1.56% below the 6% Watch line
why: Cheap yen borrowing funds positions worldwide; a sharp yen rally forces those trades to unwind, as in the global sell-off of August 2024.
drivers: Bank of Japan policy, the US–Japan rate gap, JGB yields, currency intervention, risk appetite.

rubric.alert: A move of more than 5% in a week or 10% in a month, with stress spreading to other markets.
rubric.watch: A 3–5% move in a week, a 6–10% move in a month, or Japanese currency intervention.
rubric.normal: The yen moves less than 3% against the dollar in a week and less than 6% in a month.
